## Overview

This project is a **working RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) application** you can run on your laptop. It answers questions by **searching a document library first**, then building an answer from what was retrieved — with **source titles and categories** listed in every response.

Unlike a generic chatbot that guesses, this app **grounds** every answer in your knowledge base. You can run the **same question through three retrieval strategies** and compare how results change.

**GitHub:** [sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project](https://github.com/sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project)

**Stack:** Python · scikit-learn (TF-IDF) · NetworkX · Flask

## What it does (plain English)

| Mode | What happens |
|------|----------------|
| **Naive** | One search → top matches → answer |
| **Advanced** | Rewrite the question → search → rerank → answer |
| **Graph** | Advanced pipeline + pull related docs via a knowledge graph → answer |

Generic chatbots often **guess**. This app **looks up** short policy-style documents (AI/ML, data science, IT operations, manufacturing, research) and builds an answer only from what was retrieved.

## Background of the Study

Teams deploying internal Q&A over PDFs, wikis, and runbooks hit the same wall: a single “vector search + LLM” pipeline misses nuance. **Query wording** matters, **keyword vs semantic match** both matter, and **related documents** (same category, linked topics) often hold the missing context.

This project isolates those ideas in a **small, transparent codebase** — no black-box hosted stack required for the demo. TF-IDF stands in for dense embeddings so results are fast and reproducible on any machine; the **graph layer** shows how category-linked expansion can surface extra evidence before the answer is formed.

## Motivation of the Study

- **Compare pipelines fairly** — same corpus, same question, three modes
- **Show why “advanced RAG” exists** — rewrite + rerank beats one-shot search on several test questions
- **Demonstrate graph-augmented retrieval** — category nodes connect documents for broader context
- **Ship something runnable** — CLI demo, comparison script, and REST API for integration tests
- **Portfolio clarity** — clone, run, and inspect the logic in minutes

## Project structure

```text
rag-capstone-graduation-project/
│
├── data/
│   └── knowledge_base.json      ← 10 domain documents (your corpus)
│
├── src/
│   ├── retriever.py             ← Load docs, TF-IDF search, knowledge graph
│   └── pipeline.py              ← Three modes: naive / advanced / graph
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── run_demo.py              ← Print all three modes for one question
│   └── compare_modes.py         ← Compare modes on sample questions → JSON report
│
├── outputs/
│   └── mode_comparison.json     ← Generated comparison report
│
├── app.py                       ← Flask REST API (port 8093)
├── requirements.txt             ← flask, scikit-learn, numpy, networkx
└── README.md
```

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `data/knowledge_base.json` | Document corpus — id, title, category, text |
| `src/retriever.py` | TF-IDF search + NetworkX knowledge graph |
| `src/pipeline.py` | Query rewrite, rerank, graph expand, answer builder |
| `scripts/run_demo.py` | Quick visual test — all modes on one question |
| `scripts/compare_modes.py` | Batch comparison → `outputs/mode_comparison.json` |
| `app.py` | REST API: `GET /health`, `GET /modes`, `POST /ask` |

When graph mode finds a document, it can pull in **another document from the same category** that was not already in the top results — surfacing related context before the answer is built.

### Pipeline summary (text)

```text
User question
  → mode: naive | advanced | graph
  → (optional) query rewrite
  → TF-IDF retrieval over knowledge_base.json
  → (optional) rerank by term overlap
  → (optional) graph expand via category links
  → grounded answer + source list
```

## How each part works (step by step)

### Step 1 — Knowledge base

Each record in `data/knowledge_base.json` follows this shape:

```json
{
  "id": "doc-003",
  "title": "RAG Deployment Governance",
  "category": "AI/ML",
  "text": "A production RAG system requires citation checks..."
}
```

The built-in corpus has **10 documents** across AI/ML, data science, IT operations, manufacturing, and research — for example:

- RAG deployment governance (AI/ML)
- Feature store data quality controls (Data Science)
- Model monitoring in production (Data Science)
- Server ticket prioritization matrix (IT/IoT)
- Manufacturing traceability baseline (Manufacturing)
- Research data reproducibility standard (Research)

Add more JSON records in the same format to extend the system.

### Step 2 — Retriever (`src/retriever.py`)

This is the **search engine**.

1. **Load documents** — each doc becomes a searchable string: `title + category + text`.
2. **TF-IDF vectorization** — converts all documents and your question into vectors (fast, no GPU, easy to debug).
3. **Cosine similarity search** — returns the top-k closest documents.
4. **Knowledge graph** — NetworkX links each document to its category node (`belongs_to` edge).
5. **Graph expansion** — in graph mode, when a doc is found, pull another doc from the same category for broader context.

### Step 3 — Pipeline (`src/pipeline.py`)

This orchestrates the three modes.

**Query rewrite** (advanced + graph): adds domain keywords based on the question. For example, a question about RAG may expand with terms like *citation*, *grounding*, and *observability* to improve retrieval.

**Reranking**: boosts documents whose title and body overlap more with the query terms — not just raw TF-IDF score.

**Answer building**: produces an **extractive summary** — the top three retrieved snippets with document titles and categories cited. You can plug in Ollama or OpenAI later for generative answers.

### Step 4 — Scripts and API

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| `scripts/run_demo.py` | One question, prints all three modes side by side |
| `scripts/compare_modes.py` | Several questions → writes `outputs/mode_comparison.json` |
| `app.py` | REST API on port **8093** for health checks and `/ask` requests |

## Step-by-step — run and test locally

### Step 1 — Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project.git
cd rag-capstone-graduation-project
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Step 2 — Run the demo

```bash
python scripts/run_demo.py
```

You should see three blocks: **NAIVE**, **ADVANCED**, and **GRAPH**, each with an answer and top source title. Advanced and graph modes also show the **rewritten query** when keywords were added.

**What to expect:** advanced mode often scores higher than naive on the same question because the expanded query retrieves better matches. Graph mode may add a **related document from the same category** as a second source.

### Step 3 — Compare modes on multiple questions

```bash
python scripts/compare_modes.py
```

Writes `outputs/mode_comparison.json` and prints a table of top document and score per mode. Sample comparison output:

| Question | Naive score | Advanced score |
|----------|-------------|----------------|
| What governance is required for production RAG? | ~0.34 | ~0.47 |
| How do we prioritize server tickets? | ~0.19 | ~0.23 |

Advanced (and graph) consistently improve confidence on these test questions.

### Step 4 — Start the API

```bash
python app.py
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8093/health

curl -X POST http://localhost:8093/ask \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question":"What governance is required for production RAG?","mode":"graph"}'
```

### Step 5 — Try your own questions

Good starter questions (safe, domain-neutral demos):

- *"What governance is required for production RAG?"*
- *"How do we prioritize server tickets?"*
- *"What data quality controls should a feature store enforce?"*
- *"How should model monitoring work in production?"*

Modes: `"naive"`, `"advanced"`, or `"graph"`.

## Example API response fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `answer` | Grounded summary with cited document titles |
| `sources[]` | Ranked passages with `title`, `category`, `score`, `rerank_score` |
| `effective_query` | Expanded query (advanced/graph modes) |
| `mode` | Which pipeline ran |
| `query` | Original question |

## Advantages of this project

### 1. Educational — see RAG stages clearly

Most RAG tutorials jump straight to “vector DB + ChatGPT.” This project **separates each stage** so you can see what query rewrite, reranking, and graph expansion actually do.

### 2. Fair comparison on the same corpus

All three modes use the **same documents and the same question**. Differences come from the pipeline, not different data — ideal for learning and demos.

### 3. Runs anywhere — no GPU, no API keys

TF-IDF + scikit-learn runs on any laptop in under a second. No cloud API bill, no embedding model download required for the demo.

### 4. Transparent and debuggable

You can read every line: what was retrieved, why it was reranked, which graph neighbors were added. Production RAG systems often hide this logic.

### 5. Portfolio-ready

- Runnable in minutes (`git clone` → `pip install` → `python scripts/run_demo.py`)
- REST API for integration demos
- Covers real domains (AI/ML, data science, IT ops, manufacturing, research)
- Shows understanding of **advanced RAG** beyond basic vector search

### 6. Easy to extend

| Extension | How |
|-----------|-----|
| More documents | Add JSON records to `knowledge_base.json` |
| Better search | Swap TF-IDF for sentence-transformers in `retriever.py` |
| Generative answers | Pass retrieved contexts to Ollama or OpenAI in `build_answer()` |
| Richer graph | Add topic-to-topic edges, not just doc ↔ category |
| Web UI | Wrap `ask()` in Gradio or a simple frontend |

### 7. Shows why “advanced RAG” exists

On test questions, **advanced mode often nearly doubles the retrieval confidence score** compared to naive — just by rewriting the query. The core lesson: **how you search matters as much as what you search**.

## Limitations

- Uses **TF-IDF**, not neural embeddings — swap in sentence-transformers for production scale
- **Graph** is small (document ↔ category); not a full graph database deployment
- Answers are **extractive summaries**, not a hosted LLM — plug in Ollama or OpenAI as a next step
- Query rewrite uses **rule-based keyword expansion** — replace with an LLM rewriter for production
